title: Federal water-infrastructure assistance can be large while local affordability, service-area visibility, and maintenance remain difficult
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-25-107013 review of EPA, FEMA, and USDA assistance for drinking-water and wastewater infrastructure resilience
geography: United States; federal water-infrastructure assistance and selected utilities and communities, fiscal years 2014–2023

denominator.unit: EPA, FEMA, and USDA programs that provided or could provide financial assistance for water infrastructure and were analyzed by GAO

grant_obligations.unit: billions of U.S. dollars in grants; at least 22,000 projects

direct_loans.unit: billions of U.S. dollars in direct loans; about 4,800 projects

capitalization_grant_projects.unit: projects funded through state revolving funds during the review period

other_grant_projects.unit: projects funded by the remainder of grant programs during the review period

observations.method: GAO analyzed agency budgetary and assistance data for fiscal years 2014–2023, reviewed program documents and prior work, and assessed data reliability for the stated purposes.
observations.uncertainty: Financial obligations and project counts do not establish completed construction, operating resilience, continuity of water service, household affordability, or disaster performance.
observations.subgroup: EPA, FEMA, and USDA programs; rural, low-income, and other communities identified as vulnerable under differing statutory or program definitions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Large assistance totals can finance real improvements and may reduce future failures even when service continuity or household outcomes are not measured in this report.

observations.period: Selected utility interviews and EPA program analysis; review published August 2025

denominator.unit: selected drinking-water and wastewater utilities interviewed; nongeneralizable sample

local_rate_or_visibility_barriers.unit: utilities whose representatives cited local financing roadblocks such as officials denying rate increases; 2 also cited results not being readily visible to the public

maintenance_cost_barrier.unit: of 5 technical-assistance providers whose representatives said routine operations and maintenance costs were a challenge, particularly for vulnerable communities

loan_repayment_burden.unit: utilities whose representatives said federal water-infrastructure loan repayments could be costly for some communities

vulnerability_distribution.value: Clean Water State Revolving Fund analysis found communities with greater social vulnerability received about $248,000 less per community on average and high-poverty communities about $247,000 less, while communities with greater non-white or Hispanic/Latino populations received about $203,000 more on average
vulnerability_distribution.unit: average assistance association in GAO's selected statistical analysis

observations.method: GAO interviewed 14 selected utilities and technical-assistance providers, reviewed agency practices, and analyzed EPA State Revolving Fund data using water-system service-area mapping and census-tract characteristics.
observations.uncertainty: The utility interviews are not generalizable; the statistical results are associations within selected EPA programs and do not establish causal effects, project quality, completed resilience, or household water outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Selected utilities, vulnerable communities under program definitions, census tracts overlapping drinking-water or wastewater service areas, and EPA revolving-fund programs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rate resistance may reflect legitimate affordability concerns, and lower assistance in a social-vulnerability category may reflect project type, eligibility, state definitions, or service-area measurement rather than deliberate exclusion.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies assistance totals, selected utility barriers, loan repayment burdens, service-area measurement limits, and EPA program associations.

boundary: This record establishes a federal-assistance, local-finance, maintenance, and service-area measurement boundary for water-infrastructure resilience. It does not establish project completion, water quality, service continuity, household bills, health effects, disaster recovery, or public trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO accessible HTML report retrieved and hashed; underlying agency files, service-area GIS, utility records, and household water outcomes not retained
